title: Prasidh Krishna Ruled Out of New Zealand ODI Series
excerpt: The BCCI says Prasidh Krishna needs more time to build match workload as he recovers from a hamstring injury, while Mohammed Siraj joins India A for the second four-day game against New Zealand A.
body:
• Prasidh Krishna has been ruled out of India's five-match ODI series against New Zealand as he recovers from a hamstring injury, the BCCI confirmed on October 30.
  • Prasidh needs more time to build the workload required for matches and will join India A for the third four-day game, subject to clearing a Return to Play assessment.
  • Mohammed Siraj will join the India A squad for the second four-day game against New Zealand A, starting October 31.
  • Nitish Kumar Reddy stays with the ODI squad for the first ODI on November 4, then links up with India A ahead of the Test series starting November 19.

India fast bowler Prasidh Krishna has been ruled out of the five-match one-day international series against New Zealand, the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) confirmed in a media advisory on October 30, in an update also reported by the ICC.

Prasidh's availability for the series had been subject to fitness clearance. The right-arm pacer is recovering from a hamstring injury and, the BCCI said, will need additional time to build up the workload required to be ready for matches. No replacement announcement for the ODI squad was made in the advisory; instead, the board set out a staged return through India A.

A staged return through India A

Prasidh will join the India A squad for the third and final four-day game against New Zealand A, subject to him clearing the Return to Play (RTP) assessment. The BCCI said the stint would give him an opportunity to gain match practice and prepare for the Test series that follows the one-day matches.

That sequence — assessment first, red-ball match practice second, Test consideration after — tells its own story about where Prasidh sits in his recovery. The board is not closing the door on the two-match Test series against New Zealand, which begins on November 19, but it is no longer planning around him for the 50-over leg of the tour.

Siraj and Reddy shuffled for red-ball preparation

Mohammed Siraj, who is named in India's ODI squads for the series, will meanwhile join the India A squad for the second four-day game, starting October 31, 2026, against New Zealand A. The BCCI listed him in India A's updated squad for that match, captained by Dhruv Jurel, alongside Yashasvi Jaiswal, Sai Sudharsan, Devdutt Padikkal, Washington Sundar and Akash Deep, among others.

Nitish Kumar Reddy follows a similar path on a delayed timeline. He will remain part of the ODI squad for the first ODI against New Zealand, to be played on November 4, 2026, and will then link up with the India A squad for the third and final four-day game. The ICC noted the move will give Reddy match practice ahead of the two-match ICC World Test Championship series against New Zealand starting November 19.

The ODI squads after the update

For the first three ODIs, India are led by Shubman Gill, with Shreyas Iyer as vice-captain and a squad including Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, KL Rahul, Axar Patel, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Arshdeep Singh, Ishan Kishan, Mohammed Siraj and Kuldeep Yadav, with Reddy available only for the first ODI. For the fourth and fifth ODIs, Iyer captains the side, with Tilak Varma, Auqib Nabi, Kumar Kushagra and Yash Thakur among those coming in.

The series opens on November 4 in Auckland, followed by matches on November 7 in Wellington, November 10 in Hamilton, and November 13 and 15 in Mount Maunganui, according to the ICC schedule. India's pace planning for those games now proceeds without Prasidh, while his own focus shifts to the RTP assessment and the India A four-day game that could put him back in Test contention.
